# Parse-and-gap

**Status:** specced, not built.
**Article:** [Finding Your Next Job, with AI](/aging-well/next-job.md) — plan three, "the two documents."
**Precedent:** [`budget-from-statements`](/aging-well/budget-from-statements.md) — a browser tab, your own files, nothing uploaded.

## What it does

You paste (or upload) two things: your master résumé, as `portfolio.yaml`
from [resume-typst](https://github.com/eLearningHub/resume-typst), and a job
posting. The tool answers three questions, in order:

1. **What does a parser see?** Render the résumé through the same
   single-column, no-table layout an ATS actually reads, so a two-column
   sidebar résumé's silent failures — a phone number that never parses, a
   skills column that comes out as one run-on line — are visible before you
   send it anywhere.
2. **What's the keyword gap?** Compare the posting's stated requirements to
   the résumé's content, line by line: strong / partial / missing, each
   citing the `evidence.md` entry behind it. Never invents a match.
3. **A tailored draft.** Reorders and rephrases — never adds — bullets to fit
   the posting's vocabulary, subject to the fabrication guard below, and
   renders both layouts (human, parser) as PDF.

## The fabrication guard

Every bullet in `portfolio.yaml` carries a `source:` field pointing at a
line in the reader's `evidence.md`. A bullet the tool proposes with no
traceable source doesn't render — this is the one hard rule, borrowed from
two small open-source projects that treat it as a design constraint
(`ats-resume-agent`, `imprintcv` — see the
[GitHub research](/aging-well/research/github-open-source.md#2-resume--cv-tailoring-and-ats-matching-with-llms)).

## Built on resume-typst

[eLearningHub/resume-typst](https://github.com/eLearningHub/resume-typst)
already keeps résumé *content* in `portfolio.yaml` and *look* in
`settings.yaml`, rendered by [Typst](https://typst.org/). It needs four
changes before this tool can be built on it — see
[the research report](/aging-well/research/next-job-with-ai.md#building-on-resume-typst)
for the full rationale:

- A single-column `ats.typ` entry file alongside the existing two-column
  `main.typ`, same YAML.
- The hard-coded summary paragraph and link labels moved out of `main.typ`
  and into `portfolio.yaml`.
- A `source:` field per bullet (the fabrication guard above).
- Typst compiled to WebAssembly ([typst.ts](https://github.com/Myriad-Dreamin/typst.ts))
  so rendering happens in the tab — no upload to typst.app.

## Open

- Where the posting's text comes from: pasted by the reader, or fetched from
  a URL client-side (CORS permitting)?
- Whether the parser-view step needs a real ATS parsing library or a
  faithful approximation is enough to make the point.
